gloss: to get angry; to lose one's temper

definitions.gloss: to get angry; to be infuriated; to lose one's temper
definitions.explanation: To become angry, said of a sudden flare-up rather than a slow build. Literally 'it comes to the head.' Colloquial and forceful, used mainly about oneself in casual speech.

examples.japanese: ⟦その→その：00993_sono⟧⟦{言|い}い{方|かた}→言い方：14165_iikata⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{頭|あたま}に{来|き}た。
examples.english: The way he said that made me angry.

examples.japanese: ⟦{約束|やくそく}→約束：01517_yakusoku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{破|やぶ}られて→破る：02321_yaburu⟧⟦{本当|ほんとう}→本当：00779_hontou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{頭|あたま}に{来|き}た。
examples.english: I was really furious that they broke their promise.

examples.japanese: {頭|あたま}に{来|き}たとき⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{一度|いちど}→一度：01312_ichido⟧⟦{深呼吸|しんこきゅう}→深呼吸：13294_shinkokyuu⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ようにして⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: When I get angry, I make a point of taking one deep breath.

examples.japanese: ⟦{何度|なんど}→何度：17592_nando⟧⟦{注意|ちゅうい}→注意：01464_chuui⟧⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{同|おな}じ→同じ：02857_onaji⟧⟦ミス→ミス：00285_misu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧くり{返|かえ}す⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、さすが⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{頭|あたま}に{来|き}てしまった。
examples.english: He kept making the same mistake no matter how often I warned him, so I finally lost my temper.

notes:
STRUCTURE: ⟦{頭|あたま}→頭：00574_atama⟧ (head) + ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ + ⟦{来|く}る→来る：00254_kuru⟧ (to come). The past {頭|あたま}に{来|き}た is by far the most common form.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {頭|あたま}に{来|き}た: I got angry
- 〜⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{頭|あたま}に{来|く}る: to get angry at ~
- {頭|あたま}に{来|き}て⟦{何|なに}も→何も：03874_nanimo⟧⟦{言|い}えなかった→言う：00515_iu⟧: to be too angry to speak

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{腹|はら}が{立|た}つ→腹が立つ：06886_haragatatsu⟧: to get angry — the standard, less charged expression, usable in writing
- ムカつく: to be pissed off — slangier and younger-sounding
- ⟦{怒|おこ}る→怒る：00876_okoru⟧: to get angry, to scold — the plain verb; also covers telling someone off

USAGE:
Too casual for business or formal writing; use ⟦{腹|はら}が{立|た}つ→腹が立つ：06886_haragatatsu⟧ there. Said of another person it can sound accusatory, so it usually describes the speaker's own reaction.
